title: Yonder Tech — IT enablement & digital consulting, Auckland
description: Yonder Tech works with New Zealand businesses on IT strategy, system integration, data platforms and managed operations.

hero.lede: Yonder Tech works with New Zealand businesses and delivery partners on the unglamorous half of digital transformation: deciding what to build, integrating what already exists, and proving the result in numbers a board recognises.

work.heading: Nine concepts. Four to start with.
work.lede: Self-directed concept work. Each entry carries its brief, the decisions that shaped it, and the design system it delivered.

rows.title: Luna Bloom Society maternity community
rows.body: A community that holds long-form editorial and peer conversation without an endless feed: complete story sets, small trimester rooms, no engagement counters.
rows.alt: Luna Bloom Society maternity community concept

rows.title: Ion Forge X9 product launch system
rows.body: A hardware launch system carrying industrial design, spec detail and motion in one view, then repeating across twelve markets without a rebuild.
rows.alt: Ion Forge X9 product launch concept

rows.title: Northbridge Capital research hub
rows.body: A daily-publishing research hub that absorbs editorial volume without reading as a link dump. Identical card space; hierarchy from imagery and category.

rows.title: Atlas Capital institutional experience
rows.body: One confident statement, one audited number stated with its as-of date, and a leadership interview module in place of stock photography.

work.note: Concept projects designed in-house, not client engagements. Figures describe the delivered design system, not commercial results.

capabilities.heading: Four things we do, and nothing we don't.

items.title: IT strategy & architecture governance
items.body: A technology roadmap tied to the commercial plan, with a decision record for every choice, so the next person can see why.

items.title: System integration & platform build
items.body: Connecting what you already run before proposing anything new. Fewer systems, fewer manual bridges, one consistent record.

items.title: Data platforms & applied AI
items.body: Agreed metric definitions first, automation second, models only where the decision they support is worth the maintenance.

items.title: Operations & continuous optimisation
items.body: Someone accountable after go-live: run-books, service levels and a quarterly review that reports against the original measure.

method.heading: Two weeks to a decision you can defend.
method.photoAlt: Meeting room in an office tower

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.body: Two weeks, fixed fee. Systems, data, cost and the three constraints that actually block you.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body: A costed roadmap with sequencing, a measure per stage, and the option to stop after any one of them.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.body: Our team or yours, with the same named lead from diagnosis through to the quarterly review.

insights.heading: Written for the person signing the invoice.

cards.title: What a technology roadmap owes the board
cards.body: Three questions a roadmap has to answer before it is worth presenting: what stops, what starts, and what it costs to be wrong.

cards.title: The case against replacing your ERP
cards.body: Most integration pain is process pain wearing a technical costume. How to tell the difference before committing to a migration.

cards.title: Metrics before models
cards.body: Why the first automation project should be the one nobody wants to demo, and how to sequence the rest behind it.

contact.body: A 60-minute review, then a fixed-fee fortnight. You leave with a costed roadmap and no obligation to continue.
